name: Inventory replenishment capability evolution (demo)
description: Synthetic demonstration of a replenishment workflow that begins with AI-assisted exploration, keeps purchase orders human-approved, and promotes stable analysis into governed software tools while AI continues to find operational gaps.
processNode: Daily replenishment review before a planner decides whether to approve a purchase-order draft.
decisionOrAction: Recommend whether and how much to replenish, explain the evidence and uncertainty, and prepare a purchase-order draft for human review without submitting it.

metrics.name: Preventable stockout exposure
metrics.definition: Count of product-days where forecast available stock falls below expected demand before replenishment can arrive and the condition was visible early enough to review.
metrics.target: proposed:reduce preventable exposure during shadow operation

metrics.name: Planner correction rate
metrics.definition: Share of recommendations whose quantity, timing, supplier, or reason is materially changed by the planner before approval.
metrics.target: proposed:decline after stable logic is promoted into tools

ontologyReferences.purpose: Proposed definitions for product, available stock, demand, inbound supply, lead time, replenishment recommendation, purchase-order draft, and planner correction.

sourceReferences.purpose: Current on-hand, reserved, and inbound quantities with freshness and provenance.
Historical sales and approved promotion calendar used to estimate near-term demand pressure.
Declared and observed supplier lead time, minimum order quantity, and delivery variability.

acceptanceCriteria: Each recommendation identifies its source evidence, freshness, semantic or tool version, uncertainty, and access decision.
The assistant prepares only a purchase-order draft and cannot approve, submit, or write it without a named human approval and governed system action.
Planner changes and reasons are recorded so repeated corrections can become candidates for a versioned rule, model, semantic, process, or control change.
A stable candidate is promoted only after replay or shadow evidence, accountable owner acceptance, tests, versioning, rollout, and rollback are defined.
notes: This record is proposed and synthetic. Real owners, baselines, source authority, access decisions, thresholds, and acceptance evidence are missing.
